chunks: Al-Hasan ibn Muhammad ibn Sama'ah narrated from Wuhayb ibn Hafs, from Abi Basir, from Abi 'Abdillah عليه السلام, who said:

The salat in residence is eight rak'ahs when the sun passes the meridian; the time between that and the passing of two-thirds of a qamah is for you, and when two-thirds of a qamah has passed, you begin with the obligatory prayer.

key_terms.اَلصَّلَاةُ: salat; here referring to the prescribed cycle of prayer discussed in timing
key_terms.بِالْفَرِيضَةِ: with the obligatory prayer; meaning the required salat is then to be started
key_terms.ثَمَانِي رَكَعَاتٍ: eight rak'ahs; the recommended units prayed before the obligatory prayer
key_terms.ثُلُثَا الْقَامَةِ: two-thirds of a qamah; a traditional measure used to determine prayer timing
key_terms.زَالَتِ الشَّمْسُ: the sun declined from the meridian; the beginning of the relevant prayer time
key_terms.فِي الْحَضَرِ: while in residence, as opposed to travel

ai.seo_question: When should the eight rak'ahs before Zuhr be performed in residence, and when does the obligatory prayer begin?
ai.summary: This hadith explains the time for performing the eight rak'ahs of nawafil prayer in residence after zawal. It indicates that these are performed from the sun's decline until two-thirds of a qamah has passed, after which one should begin the obligatory prayer.
